sources.locator: "War in Donbas", revision 1370749630, lead and § Protests in the Donbas

explanation: The article runs the one into the other. Its § Protests in the Donbas opens “Following the revolution, counter-revolutionary and pro-Russian protests began in parts of the Donbas” and, of 6 April, “demonstrators in Donetsk demanded a referendum on autonomy or accession to Russia”. Six days later “unmarked pro-Russian militants seized the Donetsk headquarters of the Interior Ministry and two police stations without resistance”, which is where this record begins. The edge is `enabled`. The protests are the ground the armed seizures were made on, and no order to make them. The lead names “Russian-backed paramilitaries” as those who fought it.
